harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Formed a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster (node1, node2, node3 on RHEL 9) with a payments vhost, an app_user account scoped to that vhost, and a durable quorum queue "orders" replicated across all three nodes. Verified messages survive the loss of any one node and remain consumable from the survivors. Completed the mandatory rolling-restart protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed boot identities and full cluster/data recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang and rabbitmq-server via official packagecloud repos on node1, node2, node3
Added CLUSTER_HOSTS entries to /etc/hosts and opened firewalld ports 4369/5672/15672/25672/35672-35682 on all nodes
Set up cluster SSH keys; generated a random Erlang cookie on node1 with openssl and distributed it via scp to node2 and node3
Started and enabled rabbitmq-server on all nodes; enabled rabbitmq_management plugin
Joined node2 and node3 to node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; verified 3-node disk cluster with no partitions
Created payments vhost and app_user account (randomly generated password) with configure/write/read permissions scoped only to that vhost
Declared durable quorum queue 'orders' (x-queue-type=quorum, replicated across all 3 nodes) via AMQP (pika) as app_user

Published 5 durable messages, stopped rabbitmq-server on the leader node (node1), confirmed leader failover to node3 with quorum intact and message count preserved, then consumed all 5 messages successfully from node2 while node1 was down
Restarted node1's rabbitmq-server service and confirmed the node rejoined the 3-node cluster
Republished 5 durable messages as a fresh baseline and captured boot_id plus rabbitmq-server active status baseline on all 3 nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 (one at a time) using systemctl reboot, polling each node until reachable again

After each reboot, verified a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, rabbitmq-server active, all 3 cluster nodes running, and the orders queue retaining all 5 messages across all 3 replicas before proceeding to the next node
After all three restarts, consumed all 5 messages from node2 to prove end-to-end functionality and confirmed payments vhost and app_user permissions were intact

evidence.summary: join_cluster run on node2 and node3 against node1; cluster_status on node1 shows all 3 as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with no partitions
add_vhost payments succeeded; list_vhosts post-restart confirms payments still present

evidence.requirement: application account can publish and consume in payments vhost
evidence.summary: app_user created with configure/write/read '.*' permissions on payments; used successfully to publish and consume messages; permissions verified intact after restarts

evidence.requirement: durable queue replicated so messages survive loss of one node and stay consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: Quorum queue 'orders' declared durable with members on all 3 nodes; 5 durable messages published; node1 (queue leader) stopped via systemctl stop; cluster_status/list_queues from node2 show node1 down, quorum leader failed over to node3, message count still 5; all 5 messages successfully consumed from node2 while node1 was down

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence (baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dd772e5e...; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; new boot_id 57c06111... confirms restart; rabbitmq-server active and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running; orders queue shows 5 messages across all 3 members post-recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence (baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5f3ce3b8...; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; new boot_id 4a1085ac... confirms restart; rabbitmq-server active and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, orders queue retains 5 messages

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence (baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 910dc564...; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; new boot_id de6778d8... confirms restart; rabbitmq-server active and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, orders queue retains 5 messages with new leader elected; final consume from node2 retrieves all 5 messages confirming full recovery
